stem: Best guess: which is a deduction for AGI (an adjustment)?

choices.text: The deductible half of self-employment tax
choices.explanation: Correct. Half of SE tax is an above-the-line adjustment.

explanation: Half of SE tax is an above-the-line adjustment.

stem: The 2025 educator expense cap is $300. A public school teacher spent $450 on classroom supplies in 2025. What is the educator expense adjustment?

choices.explanation: Correct. Educator expense deduction: up to $300 per eligible educator.
Eligible educators may deduct up to $300.

explanation: Educator expense deduction: up to $300 per eligible educator.

stem: The 2025 phase-out range for a single filer is MAGI $85,000–$100,000. Single taxpayer, MAGI $95,000, paid $2,500 of student loan interest. What is the deduction?

For 2025 the HSA contribution limit for family coverage is $8,550, and an additional $1,000 catch-up is allowed at age 55 or older. What is the maximum contribution for a 45-year-old with family high-deductible coverage?

choices.explanation: Includes a catch-up she isn't eligible for (55+).
Correct. 2025 HSA limits: $4,300 self-only, $8,550 family; +$1,000 catch-up at 55.

explanation: 2025 HSA limits: $4,300 self-only, $8,550 family; +$1,000 catch-up at 55.

stem: The 2025 IRA contribution limit is $7,000, plus a $1,000 catch-up at age 50 or older. A 52-year-old single taxpayer not covered by any employer plan contributes to a traditional IRA in 2025. What is the maximum deduction (with enough earned income)?

choices.explanation: No phase-out applies without plan coverage.

explanation: Not an active participant → fully deductible at any income; 2025 limit $7,000 + $1,000 at 50+.

stem: Which item is **not** an adjustment to income for 2025?

choices.text: Moving expenses of a civilian employee
choices.explanation: Correct. Only Armed Forces members may deduct moving expenses.

choices.text: Penalty on early withdrawal of savings
HSA contributions made by the individual

explanation: Moving expense deductions are limited to active-duty military moving under orders.

stem: A self-employed taxpayer has net SE income of $40,000 and pays $9,000 of health insurance premiums; she isn't eligible for any employer plan. What is the deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. §162(l): self-employed health insurance is deductible for AGI up to net SE income.

choices.text: $9,000 as an itemized medical expense only

choices.explanation: There is no 50% limit on this deduction.

explanation: §162(l): self-employed health insurance is deductible for AGI up to net SE income.

stem: For 2025 the IRA limit is $7,000, and the deduction phases out for joint filers who are both active participants between MAGI $126,000 and $146,000. A married couple filing jointly, both covered by workplace plans, has MAGI of $150,000. How much traditional IRA contribution can each deduct?
explanation: Joint phase-out for active participants: $126,000–$146,000 in 2025.

stem: Which taxpayer can't deduct student loan interest?

choices.text: A single taxpayer with MAGI of $60,000
A joint filer with MAGI of $150,000
A taxpayer who paid $1,000 of interest
choices.explanation: The amount paid doesn't bar the deduction.

explanation: Married filing separately and dependents can't take the student loan interest deduction.

stem: An individual withdraws a CD early and forfeits $300 of interest. How is the penalty treated?

choices.explanation: Correct. The full interest is reported, and the forfeited penalty is an adjustment.

explanation: The full interest is reported, and the forfeited penalty is an adjustment.

stem: Why is it usually better for a deduction to be an adjustment rather than an itemized deduction?

choices.text: Adjustments reduce AGI and are available even with the standard deduction
choices.explanation: Correct. Adjustments benefit all taxpayers and lower AGI-based limits.

explanation: Adjustments benefit all taxpayers and lower AGI-based limits.

stem: For 2025 the deduction phases out for a single active participant between MAGI $79,000 and $89,000. A single taxpayer covered by an employer plan has MAGI of $84,000 and contributes $7,000 to a traditional IRA. What is the deductible amount?
Employer HSA contributions for an employee are:

choices.text: Included in wages and deductible by the employee
Excluded from the employee's income and counted toward the annual limit
choices.explanation: Correct. Employer contributions are excluded from income but reduce the employee's remaining contribution room.
HSA contributions aren't taxed that way.

explanation: Employer contributions are excluded from income but reduce the employee's remaining contribution room.

stem: A self-employed taxpayer with AGI of $80,000 (as prepared) paid $7,200 of health insurance premiums and was not eligible for an employer plan. The preparer included the premiums in itemized medical expenses. What is the effect of correcting the return?

choices.explanation: 1,200 is the medical deduction above the 7.5% floor (7,200 − 6,000); the adjustment is the full premium.

choices.text: AGI is unchanged; itemized deductions fall
choices.explanation: The premiums belong above the line, so AGI does change.
There is no 50% limit on the self-employed health insurance deduction.
Correct. Self-employed health insurance is deducted for AGI under §162(l), so the full 7,200 comes off AGI and is removed from itemized medical expenses.

explanation: Moving a deduction above the line also changes every AGI-based floor and phase-out computed afterward.

stem: For 2025, eligible educators may deduct up to $300 of classroom expenses for AGI. A teacher spends $450. What is her adjustment?

choices.explanation: Correct. The deduction is capped at $300.

explanation: Eligible educators deduct up to $300 of unreimbursed classroom expenses as an adjustment to income.

stem: Which alimony payment is deductible by the payer?

choices.explanation: Correct. Pre-2019 instruments keep the old rules.
They must be required by an instrument.

explanation: Alimony is deductible only under divorce or separation instruments executed before 2019 (and not modified to adopt the new rules).

stem: A single taxpayer below the phaseout range paid $3,200 of qualified student loan interest. What is the adjustment?

choices.explanation: Correct. The deduction is capped at $2,500.
The cap isn't half the interest.

explanation: The student loan interest deduction is limited to $2,500 per return, subject to an AGI phaseout.

stem: A sole proprietor contributes to her own SEP-IRA. Where is the contribution deducted?

choices.text: As an expense on Schedule C
choices.explanation: Contributions for herself aren't on Schedule C.
Correct. It isn't a Schedule C expense.

explanation: Contributions to a self-employed person's own SEP are deducted as an adjustment to income, not on Schedule C (employee contributions are).

stem: Which taxpayer may contribute to an HSA for 2025?

choices.text: One enrolled in Medicare Part A
One covered only by a high-deductible plan
One also covered by a low-deductible plan

explanation: HSA eligibility requires HDHP coverage, no disqualifying other coverage, no Medicare enrollment and not being a dependent.

stem: A self-employed taxpayer could have joined his spouse's employer-subsidized health plan all year but bought his own policy instead. Can he deduct the premiums as an adjustment?

choices.text: Yes, up to his SE earnings
choices.explanation: Eligibility for another plan bars it.

choices.text: Yes, as an itemized deduction only
No, eligibility for the spouse's plan bars it
choices.explanation: Correct. Monthly eligibility for a subsidized plan disallows it.

choices.text: Yes, if he pays with business funds

explanation: The self-employed health insurance deduction isn't allowed for months the taxpayer is eligible for a subsidized employer plan, including a spouse's.

stem: A single taxpayer with MAGI of $200,000 isn't covered by any workplace retirement plan. How much of a $7,000 traditional IRA contribution is deductible?

choices.explanation: The phaseout applies to active participants.
Correct. No phaseout applies without plan coverage.

explanation: If neither the taxpayer nor a spouse is an active participant, the traditional IRA deduction isn't phased out.

stem: A married couple filing jointly, both age 40, has $50,000 of wages earned by one spouse. What is their maximum combined IRA contribution for 2025?

choices.explanation: Correct. A spousal IRA allows $7,000 each.
The nonworking spouse can contribute too.

explanation: A spousal IRA lets a nonworking spouse contribute up to the limit if joint earned income covers both contributions.

stem: For 2025, who may deduct moving expenses as an adjustment to income?

choices.text: Any employee moving 50 miles for work

choices.explanation: Correct. The deduction is otherwise suspended.

choices.text: Retirees moving to a new state

explanation: For 2025, only members of the Armed Forces on active duty moving under military orders may deduct moving expenses.

stem: In 2025 a married couple files jointly with MAGI of $241,000. Only the wife is covered by a workplace plan. The husband contributes $7,000 to a traditional IRA. The phaseout range for a noncovered spouse is $236,000–$246,000. How much can he deduct?

choices.explanation: A phaseout applies via his spouse.
Correct. He is halfway through the $10,000 range.

explanation: A noncovered spouse's deduction phases out over $236,000–$246,000 when the other spouse is covered.

stem: A single taxpayer pays $2,500 of student loan interest. Her 2025 MAGI is $92,500; the phaseout is $85,000–$100,000. What is her deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. Half of the range is exceeded.

explanation: The deduction is reduced proportionally across the MAGI range.

stem: A self-employed taxpayer has $6,000 of net SE profit and $424 of deductible SE tax. He pays $9,000 of health insurance premiums. What is his SE health insurance deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. Limited to net SE earnings less half the SE tax.

explanation: The self-employed health insurance deduction can't exceed earned income from the business, net of the SE tax deduction.

stem: A 2017 divorce decree was modified in 2022 and the modification expressly adopted the post-2018 alimony rules. Is the alimony deductible in 2025?

choices.explanation: Correct. The modification brought it under the new rules.

explanation: Pre-2019 instruments modified to expressly adopt the TCJA rules lose the deduction.

stem: A taxpayer cashes a CD early, forfeiting $1,000 of interest; the CD earned $600 of interest that year. How much may she deduct as an early withdrawal penalty?

choices.explanation: Correct. The full penalty is deductible, even above the year's interest.

explanation: Penalties on early withdrawal of savings are deductible for AGI in full.

stem: A married couple filing jointly are both K–12 teachers. One spent $450 on classroom supplies and the other $100. What is their educator expense deduction?
explanation: The $300 educator expense limit applies per eligible educator.

stem: An employee with $180,000 of wages (above the $176,100 wage base) also has $50,000 of net SE income. What is the deductible half of her SE tax?

choices.explanation: Correct. Only the 2.9% Medicare portion applies: $46,175 × 2.9% ÷ 2.
The Social Security portion is already maxed.

explanation: Wages up to the base reduce the SE earnings subject to the 12.4% Social Security tax.

stem: A taxpayer contributes to her traditional IRA on April 10, 2026 and designates it for 2025. When is it deductible?

choices.explanation: Correct. Contributions by the filing due date count for the prior year.

explanation: IRA contributions made by the return due date (without extensions) may count for the prior year.

stem: An employee's employer puts $3,000 into her family HSA in 2025 (family limit $8,550). How much can she deduct for her own contributions?

choices.explanation: Correct. Employer contributions count toward the limit.

explanation: Employer HSA contributions are excluded from income and reduce the employee's remaining limit.

stem: A sole proprietor has $100,000 of net SE profit and $7,065 of deductible SE tax. What is her maximum SEP contribution deduction?

choices.explanation: Subtract half the SE tax first.

explanation: For self-employed people, the 25% SEP limit works out to 20% of net SE earnings after the SE tax deduction.

stem: For 2025, what is the maximum educator expense deduction for an eligible teacher?

choices.explanation: Correct. Educator expenses are capped at $300.

explanation: Eligible educators may deduct up to $300 of unreimbursed classroom expenses as an adjustment to income.

stem: Where does a self-employed individual deduct health insurance premiums?

choices.explanation: It's an adjustment for the self-employed.

choices.text: As a Schedule C business expense

explanation: Self-employed health insurance is deducted above the line, limited to net self-employment earnings.

stem: What is the maximum annual student loan interest deduction?
explanation: Taxpayers may deduct up to $2,500 of student loan interest, subject to an income phase-out.
